title: Commercial Property Due Diligence in Newcastle: Evidence to Request Before You Buy
excerpt: Organise property documents, planning questions, lease evidence and specialist inspection scopes before a Newcastle commercial purchase.
content:
Commercial property due diligence starts with the intended use of the premises and a record of the evidence needed to assess that particular property. For a Newcastle or Hunter business, the advertised price, floor area and rent summary do not answer every operational, contractual or condition question.

This guide is a preparation checklist for discussions with your appointed advisers. It does not provide a valuation, building inspection, approval assessment or legal, tax, financial, credit or investment advice.

## Start with the buying brief

Describe how the business will use the premises: staff, visitors, equipment, deliveries, storage and any proposed works. Keep essential requirements separate from preferences so each opportunity is tested against the same brief.

If the property is tenanted, distinguish your occupation plans from the existing tenancy arrangements. Ask your solicitor how the documents affect the proposed purchase and intended use. Do not assume that an advertised availability date resolves those questions.

[Prepare a commercial property buying brief](/blog/commercial-buyers-agent-brief-newcastle)

## Build an evidence and responsibility register

Request available documents through the selling agent and your appointed team. Record what is missing, who will investigate it and how it affects the decision. A document being supplied is not the same as a specialist having reviewed it.

| Workstream | Evidence to discuss | Adviser question |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contract and title | Contract, title information, relevant interests and conditions | What needs clarification or protection in the actual documents? |
| Planning and use | Planning information, available consents and the proposed activities | What applies to this site and proposed use? |
| Existing leases | Complete leases, variations, side agreements and available tenancy records | What do the actual terms and records mean for the purchase? |
| Property costs | Available invoices, budgets, reconciliations and maintenance information | Which costs and assumptions belong in the comparison? |
| Building and services | Inspection scopes, service records and relevant technical documents | What is covered, excluded or still unverified? |
| Finance and valuation | Information requested by the lender, finance adviser and valuer | What further evidence, conditions or assessment is required? |

Give each open question an owner and a review date agreed with the team. Ask your solicitor which issues, conditions and deadlines need attention before you make a commitment.

## Verify planning information for the actual property

Service NSW directs property searches to the NSW Planning Portal Spatial Viewer. Use the address or lot details to begin checking the mapped planning information, then discuss the actual property and proposed activities with your planning adviser, certifier or council as appropriate.

The NSW Planning Portal also explains section 10.7 planning certificates and the information they contain. Ask your solicitor or planning adviser which current documents are needed and how they affect the transaction. Confirm the relevant council's application process, fees and processing information instead of relying on a generic turnaround claim.

A zoning label or map screenshot is not a substitute for advice on the proposed use, existing approvals or required changes. Keep the evidence and the specialist's conclusions together in the register.

## Review complete leases and property cost evidence

Where a property has tenants, obtain the complete documents available for review rather than relying only on a marketing summary. Ask your solicitor to examine the applicable rent review provisions, options, dates, variations, incentives, make-good terms and other conditions relevant to the transaction.

Record the actual review mechanism and dates. Do not insert a supposed standard Newcastle rent increase into the assessment. Your valuer and lender assess the property for their particular purposes; this guide does not predict their treatment of a lease expiry, vacancy or tenant.

Compare the available property expense records with the lease documents and the scope of your advisers' work. Distinguish operating costs, unconfirmed allowances and proposed capital works. Ask what remains payable in each scenario, including any period of vacancy, rather than assuming every advertised outgoing is recoverable from a tenant.

## Commission inspections with clear scopes

Ask appropriately qualified specialists to define the investigations suitable for the building, site history and proposed use. Request written scopes, exclusions, access requirements and property-specific quotes. A report title alone does not establish that the structure, roof, mechanical equipment, electrical services, fire systems or access arrangements have all been assessed.

For asbestos, SafeWork NSW publishes guidance on workplace registers and management plans, including circumstances where a register is not required. Ask the relevant specialist what applies to the actual workplace and request the applicable records. Avoid treating the absence of one document as an automatic conclusion about every property.

Where site history or proposed activities raise environmental questions, ask an appropriately qualified environmental adviser what investigation is warranted. Do not assume the same investigation package is suitable for every industrial or commercial property.

Keep technical findings with the person responsible for interpreting them. YOS coordinates the commercial property workstream; your appointed specialists remain responsible for their disciplines.

## Connect acquisition with occupation

List the work needed after the purchase: design, approvals, appointed contractors, furniture, IT, access and moving. Keep transaction costs and occupation or project inputs visible as separate categories for review by the relevant advisers.

If works are needed, ask for a site-specific scope and programme dependencies. YOS provides client-side project management; building work is delivered by the appointed builder and trade contractors under their agreed responsibilities.

[Explore client-side FitOut project management](/office-fitout)

[Use the workplace handover checklist](/blog/office-fitout-handover-checklist)

## Questions buyers ask

### Does this checklist replace professional due diligence?

No. It helps organise the brief, documents and adviser questions. The investigations and advice needed depend on the property, proposed use and transaction.

### Can a building report be compared on price alone?

Compare the proposed scope, exclusions, specialist inputs and access arrangements as well as the quote. Ask what will remain unassessed before choosing the commission.

### Can YOS help before a property is selected?

Yes. Start with your business use, preferred locations, space and access needs, timing and questions already raised by your advisers. The commercial buying scope and fees are agreed before an engagement starts.

## Bring the brief and open questions to Joe

YOS provides commercial buyer-side support in NSW, helping organise the property brief, search, commercial due diligence inputs and negotiation. You appoint the solicitor, accountant, finance broker, valuer and technical specialists you need. YOS does not provide their professional advice or guarantee a purchase outcome.

[Explore YOS commercial buyer services](/buyers-agency)

[Discuss your property brief with Joe](/buyers-agency#buyer-enquiry)

[Download the commercial property buying brief checklist (PDF)](/guides/commercial-property-buying-checklist.pdf)

## Primary sources and scope

[Service NSW: search for planning information about a property](https://www.service.nsw.gov.au/transaction/search-for-planning-information-about-a-property)

[NSW Planning Portal: planning certificates](https://www.planningportal.nsw.gov.au/planning-certificates-list)

[SafeWork NSW: asbestos registers and management plans](https://www.safework.nsw.gov.au/resource-library/asbestos-publications/asbestos-registers-and-management-plans-fact-sheet)

These sources support the planning-information and workplace-record prompts above. They do not establish a property's suitability, a standard local market rate, inspection prices or a lender's valuation decision. Confirm the requirements for the actual property with the responsible advisers.
